input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there was nothing to read around and nothing to cite; the Background therefore contains no [REF:] citations, and I made no statement about any specific document. In place of reference-by-reference distinguishing, I built claim 1 on the combination that the disclosure itself treats as the point of the invention and that is least likely to be met by a single conventional doser: the axial ordering of land faces and port edges that makes concentrate-to-carrier isolation a geometric property rather than a control-sequence property, together with a rinse circuit whose gate is opened by the follower pin on the piston rod during the return stroke and closed again before the waist reconnects the concentrate port. A metering spool, a check valve on a dose outlet, and a flushing line are individually familiar, so the claim earns its scope from the timing relationships among them, and the Detailed Description explains the technical problem each relationship solves (back-drive toward the concentrate source, drift from retained residue, and a rinse that can be deferred or skipped) so that the argument exists in the specification before it is needed. 1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Source authority is a single USER passage, reproduced identically in input/disclosure.md and the one USER turn of input/conversation.md. input/brief.md supplies only title, applicant/inventor, "Not applicable." for cross-reference and government support, claim classes, and the preserved terminology list (metering sleeve, dose chamber, flush bypass, index collar, flush poppet, annular rinse channel) - all of which the draft honors.
4	
5	LEDGER - SUPPORTED. The great majority of the application traces cleanly. Every limitation of independent claims 1 and 13 traces to the disclosure ("The valve has a cylindrical housing with an inlet at one axial end and an outlet at the opposite axial end"; "The sleeve defines a cylindrical dose chamber, a radial concentrate port, a carrier-liquid admission port, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber"; "two axially spaced sealing lands joined by a reduced-diameter waist"; "Movement to the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port"; "the follower pin opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"; "Carrier liquid flows through an annular rinse channel between the sleeve and housing, through two radial rinse openings ... and then through the flush bypass to the outlet"; "The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port"). Dependent claims 2–8, 10–12, 14–18 and 20 likewise trace (two directed rinse openings; flexible lip on the upstream land wiping first; port/land ordering; index collar with helical cam groove indexed one increment per full stroke; three axial stop faces setting three dose volumes; spring-biased detent in one of three recesses; cartridge contents and threaded end cap; cylindrical housing with end inlet/outlet). Claim 1's generalization from "two radial rinse openings" to "at least one rinse opening" is a permissible narrowing-to-genus of a disclosed species. All 28 numerals in numerals.md are used consistently, each denotes one part, and the numerals listed on each figure sheet match the numerals the detailed description attributes to that figure. No section line is named in any view, so there is no section-designation mismatch to report. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains. The Background is prior-art framing only and cites no reference.
6	
7	LEDGER - UNTRACED (4 critical findings). Four passages of the detailed description assert matter with no affirmative USER support: (a) the actuating source for the piston rod ("a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion"); (b) the form of the one-way outlet valve ("may take any form ... such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element") - this is precisely the kind of "any form ... such as" broadening added to justify the renderer's ball-on-seat choice in FIGS. 2 and 3, and must be removed from the text rather than kept; (c) a materials-selection sentence (the disclosure says nothing about materials, and it introduces the undefined, unnumbered term "the sealing elements"); (d) structural variants of the spring-biased detent ("a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger") and of the flexible lip ("formed integrally ... or as a separate resilient element"). None of these appears anywhere in the inventor's words.
8	
9	SCOPE. The disclosure says the window "shows one of three reference numerals carried on the collar." The draft renames these throughout to "dose setting indicia," a genus broader than the disclosed species, and carries the broadened term into claims 9 and 19. Reported as a major claim_scope finding with a text-only fix; the FIG. 4 plain-patch depiction may stand as a schematic convention once the text says "numerals."
10	
11	INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (5 findings). FIG. 3 has two flow-path defects. First, the flush poppet is placed at the closed left (supply) end of the annular rinse channel, not at the flush bypass, contradicting the description and claims 1 and 13 ("a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass"); and its stem geometry is self-contradictory - the pin is "left of the inner wall," the stem's driven end is under the pin, the stem "runs leftward to a conical head," yet the head is said to sit at a seat in the transverse boss, which lies to the right of the pin. Second, FIG. 3 assigns the lower half and the upper half of one and the same annulus two different identities and two different flows ("The clear gap between the lower bands is the annular rinse channel ... The gap between the upper bands is an open passage carrying liquid to the right"), and then has the flush bypass discharge into that same annulus, so the rinse stream recirculates instead of reaching the outlet. FIG. 4 is described in 07-drawings.md as having "a portion of the housing wall broken away," but the FIG. 4 brief contains no housing wall and no break line; it instead floats an unnumbered bracket that "does not touch the collar." FIG. 4 also spaces the three detent recesses along the collar's upper silhouette and the three indicia along the visible surface - i.e., axially - although both sets are selected by rotation of the collar, so an axially spaced set cannot be indexed by "one increment" of turn and cannot present one indicium at a time to the window. Two minor items: FIG. 1 renders the inlet and outlet as downward radial stubs on the same side of the housing, in tension with "an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end" (claim 12); and FIG. 2 omits the housing wall and annular gap that FIGS. 1 and 3 show over the same region, running the admission-port tube off-sheet as though carrier liquid were supplied externally rather than from inlet 14.
12	
13	One further minor fidelity item: the description calls the carrier-liquid admission port "a radial port," a term the disclosure applies only to the concentrate port and the rinse openings.
14	
15	Total: 12 findings - 4 critical, 5 major, 3 minor. Each carries a filing-clean fix that is text- or brief-side only; no fix adds a speculative shape or optional embodiment.

18

In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.

FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.

The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the only liquid used to rinse the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.

FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall and so forms an annular space that travels with the piston 28. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke by an external actuating member, whether a hand lever, a pneumatic or hydraulic actuator, or another source of reciprocating motion. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction. The one-way outlet valve 38 may take any form that passes liquid in one direction only, such as a ball or a disc urged onto a seat, or a resiliently biased closure element.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20, where it occupies the annular space at the waist 34 and forms a measured volume of concentrate. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

lines: The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the wearing and sealing parts are replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line. The parts that contact the concentrate are the parts that are exchanged, so a change of concentrate or a worn sealing land is dealt with by fitting a further cartridge rather than by dismantling the installation.

-The materials of the metering sleeve 18, the piston 28, the flexible lip 56 and the sealing elements are selected for compatibility with the carrier liquid and with the concentrate to be dosed. The spring-biased detent 48 may be a spring-loaded ball or a spring-loaded plunger, and the flexible lip 56 may be formed integrally with the upstream sealing land 30 or as a separate resilient element retained on it.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The travel of the piston 28 on this stroke is limited by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46, which sets the measured volume.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting indicium then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. The valve is thereby left charged, rinsed and set, ready for the following cycle.

An inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable measured volume of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid and rinses the surfaces that contacted the concentrate after each dose, without electrical power and without any command additional to the stroke that delivers the dose.

The valve has a housing with an inlet and an outlet and a metering sleeve fixed within the housing. The metering sleeve defines a dose chamber, a concentrate port opening into the dose chamber, a carrier-liquid admission port opening into the dose chamber, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber. A piston slides axially in the dose chamber between a fill position and a discharge position. The piston has an upstream sealing land and a downstream sealing land axially spaced from one another and joined by a reduced-diameter waist.

Separation of the two liquids is enforced by the axial order of the land faces and the port edges rather than by the sequence in which any external command arrives. In the fill position, the waist connects the concentrate port to the dose chamber while the upstream and downstream sealing lands isolate the carrier-liquid admission port from the concentrate port. Movement of the piston toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream sealing land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port. Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume of concentrate and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve toward the outlet. Because one land face has passed the concentrate port before the other land face releases the carrier-liquid admission port, no position of the piston places the concentrate source in communication with the carrier-liquid path.

The rinse is carried out by the return of the same piston. An annular rinse channel lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing, and at least one rinse opening leads from that channel through the metering sleeve into the dose chamber. A follower pin carried by the piston rod opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass during the return stroke, so that carrier liquid sweeps the annular rinse channel, issues from the rinse opening across the surfaces wetted by the concentrate, and leaves through the flush bypass to the outlet. The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port to the dose chamber, so the rinse is complete, and the rinse liquid is on its way to the outlet, before any further concentrate can enter. The rinse cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred, because the element that opens it is the element that carries the piston.

In described embodiments, a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wipes the wall of the dose chamber before the flush poppet opens, so that the flushing stream is presented with a film rather than with standing liquid. Two radial rinse openings are directed across the concentrate port and across the one-way outlet valve, which are the two surfaces on which residue is otherwise retained.

Dose selection is mechanical and self-indexing. An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin, so that each full stroke of the piston turns the index collar by one increment. Three selectable axial stop faces on the index collar limit the travel of the piston and thereby set three dose volumes, a spring-biased detent engaging one of three recesses retains the selected setting, and a transparent window in the housing shows one of three dose setting indicia carried by the index collar, so that the setting is visible without electronics.

A replaceable cartridge contains the piston, the metering sleeve, the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, and is retained by a threaded end cap. Removing the threaded end cap withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the connections at the inlet and the outlet.

A corresponding method admits concentrate to the dose chamber, closes the concentrate port before uncovering the carrier-liquid admission port, expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve, and then opens the flush poppet with the follower pin during the return of the piston and closes it again before the concentrate port is reconnected.

FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting indicia 54.

The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting, so that the index collar 40 is held against vibration and against the forces transmitted through the follower pin 44 until it is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting indicia 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting indicium presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics, without power at the valve and without a controller. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the mechanism itself rather than a stored value, so the displayed setting cannot disagree with the volume that the valve will deliver.

lines: The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

41	In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting indicium then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. # FIG. 2

View: enlarged longitudinal sectional view of the metering portion of FIG. 1, axis horizontal, with the piston in the fill position. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges and margins.

Geometry:

- The metering sleeve is cut lengthwise on its axis and appears as an upper hatched wall band and a lower hatched wall band running across the width of the drawing area. The open space between them is the cylindrical dose chamber.
- An outer housing wall is cut lengthwise and appears as a hatched band above the upper sleeve band and a hatched band below the lower sleeve band, each spaced outward from the sleeve so that a clear gap runs above and below the sleeve.
- In the left portion of the dose chamber, an upstream sealing land is drawn as a hatched block whose upper and lower edges meet the bore walls; a downstream sealing land is drawn as a second such block spaced to its right; and a waist joins them, drawn as a hatched bar of smaller height on the axis, so that open space is visible between the waist and the upper bore wall and between the waist and the lower bore wall.
- A plain shaft on the axis extends leftward from the upstream sealing land and ends clear of the drawing area.
- A radial opening passes through the upper sleeve band at an axial position between the two sealing lands, its inner mouth opening into the space above the waist. A tube continues upward from it, crosses the clear gap, passes through the upper housing band and ends clear of the drawing area; the tube is shown schematically and represents the connection to a concentrate source. This opening is the concentrate port.
- A second opening passes through the lower sleeve band at the axial position of the downstream sealing land, its inner mouth covered by the lower edge of that land and its outer mouth opening into the clear gap below the sleeve. This is the carrier-liquid admission port, and it lies to the right of the concentrate port.
- To the right of the downstream sealing land, a passage rises through the upper sleeve band and widens downward into a conical seat opening into the dose chamber, with a ball resting on the seat and closing the passage. Ball and seat are shown schematically and are the one-way outlet valve, which passes liquid outward from the dose chamber.

Numerals on this sheet: 18, 20, 22, 24, 30, 32, 34, 38.

Targets:

- 18: the hatched lower sleeve band, toward the right of the view.
- 20: the open space of the dose chamber above the waist, between the two sealing lands.
- 22: interior of the opening in the upper sleeve band that opens above the waist.
- 24: interior of the opening in the lower sleeve band covered by the downstream sealing land.
- 30: hatching of the left sealing land block.
- 32: hatching of the right sealing land block.
- 34: hatching of the narrower bar joining the two blocks.
- 38: the ball resting on the conical seat.

# FIG. 3

View: enlarged longitudinal sectional view of the metering portion of FIG. 1 during the return stroke, axis horizontal, with the flush poppet held open. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges and margins.

Geometry:

- An outer housing wall cut lengthwise appears as upper and lower hatched bands along the top and bottom of the drawing area. Inside it, the sleeve wall cut lengthwise appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward from the outer bands, beginning a short way from the left and running to the right of the view. The space between the sleeve bands is the bore.
- The clear gap between the sleeve bands and the outer bands, above and below, is one annular rinse channel over the same axial extent. It is open at the left to the interior of the housing, and it is closed at its right-hand end by a hatched transverse boss that spans the gap above the sleeve and the gap below the sleeve.
- To the right of that boss, a passage leads out of the bore, up through the upper sleeve band and to the right, opening into the housing interior beyond the boss, which leads to the outlet. This passage is the flush bypass, and it carries a conical seat where it turns.
- A conical head stands clear to the left of that seat, a visible gap separating them. A stem runs leftward from the head, through an opening in the transverse boss, along the gap above the sleeve, and ends in a short flange that hangs down from the left end of the stem, beyond the left end of the sleeve. Head and stem are shown schematically and are the flush poppet, held open.
- In the bore, in the left half, the piston is drawn as two hatched enlarged portions joined by a narrower middle portion. A plain shaft extends leftward on the axis from the left portion, past the left end of the sleeve, ending clear of the drawing area. A short pin projects upward from the shaft, just right of the flange, and bears on the right face of the flange.
- At the left edge of the left enlarged portion, a thin flared projection extends up and left to touch the upper bore wall and a matching one extends down and left to the lower bore wall. These are the flexible lip.
- An opening through the upper sleeve band, at a position covered by the left enlarged portion, is the concentrate port; a tube continues upward from it, crossing the gap and the upper outer band, ending clear of the drawing area.
- Two openings through the lower sleeve band connect the annular rinse channel to the bore; they are the radial rinse openings. The left one lies directly beneath the concentrate port and is aimed at it. The right one is aimed at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper sleeve band between the concentrate port and the boss.

Numerals on this sheet: 22, 26, 28, 44, 56, 58, 60, 62.

Targets:

- 22: interior of the upper opening covered by the left portion.
- 26: interior of the flush bypass passage, right of the boss.
- 28: hatching of the right portion.
- 44: the short pin above the shaft.
- 56: the flared projection at the upper bore wall.
- 58: the conical head clear of its seat in the flush bypass at the right.

# FIG. 4

View: fragmentary side view of the index collar and the parts that set and retain the dose, collar axis horizontal. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges and margins.

Geometry:

- The index collar is drawn as a cylindrical ring seen from the side, occupying the middle of the drawing area: a long horizontal body with straight upper and lower outlines, its left end closed by a shallow curved edge indicating the round section. It surrounds an unnumbered tube, a short length of which is visible beyond the left end of the collar.
- A helical cam groove is drawn on the visible cylindrical surface as a narrow band running from the lower left of that surface to the upper right, curving gently as it wraps around the body.
- A piston rod is drawn as a plain horizontal shaft entering the view from the left on the collar axis and ending within the left part of the collar surface. A short follower pin projects radially from the end of the shaft, its outer end sitting within the narrow band of the groove.

# FIG. 3

View: enlarged longitudinal sectional view of the metering portion of FIG. 1 during the return stroke, axis horizontal, with the flush poppet held open. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges and margins.

Geometry:

- An outer housing wall appears in section as upper and lower hatched bands at the top and bottom of the drawing area. Inside it the sleeve wall appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward from them, from a short way in at the left to the right of the view. The space between the sleeve bands is the bore.
- The clear gap between the sleeve bands and the outer bands, above and below, is one annular rinse channel of the same axial extent, open at the left to the housing interior and closed at its right end by a hatched transverse boss spanning the gap above and below the sleeve.
- Right of that boss a passage leads out of the bore, up through the upper sleeve band and to the right, opening into the housing interior beyond the boss, which leads to the outlet: the flush bypass, carrying a conical seat at its turn.
- A conical head stands clear to the left of that seat, a visible gap separating them. A stem runs leftward from the head, through an opening in the boss and along the gap above the sleeve, ending in a short flange hanging down beyond the left end of the sleeve. Head and stem are shown schematically and are the flush poppet, held open.
- In the bore, in the left half, the piston is drawn as two hatched enlarged portions joined by a narrower middle portion, with a plain shaft extending leftward on the axis past the left end of the sleeve. A short pin projects upward from the shaft just right of the flange and bears on its right face.
- At the left edge of that left portion a thin flared projection extends up and left to the upper bore wall and a matching one down and left to the lower bore wall. These are the flexible lip.
- An opening through the upper sleeve band, covered by the left portion, is the concentrate port; a tube continues upward from it, crossing the gap and the upper outer band.
- Two openings through the lower sleeve band connect the annular rinse channel to the bore; they are the radial rinse openings. The left one lies beneath the concentrate port, aimed at it. The right one is aimed at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper sleeve band left of the boss.

Numerals on this sheet: 22, 26, 28, 44, 56, 58, 60, 62.

Targets:

- 22: interior of the upper opening covered by the left portion.
- 26: interior of the flush bypass, right of the boss.
- 28: hatching of the right portion.
- 44: the short pin above the shaft.
- 56: the flared projection at the upper bore wall.
- 58: the conical head clear of its seat in the flush bypass.
- 60: the clear gap between the lower bands, left of the rinse openings, the lower half of the annular rinse channel.
- 62: interior of the left lower opening.

Inside it the sleeve wall appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward from them, from a short way in at the left to the right of the view. The space between the sleeve bands is the bore.

-- The clear gap between the sleeve bands and the outer bands, above and below, is one annular rinse channel of the same axial extent, open at the left to the housing interior and closed at its right end by a hatched transverse boss spanning the gap above and below the sleeve.

-- Right of that boss a passage leads out of the bore, up through the upper sleeve band and to the right, opening into the housing interior beyond the boss, which leads to the outlet: the flush bypass, carrying a conical seat at its turn.

-- A conical head stands clear to the left of that seat, a visible gap separating them. A stem runs leftward from the head, through an opening in the boss and along the gap above the sleeve, ending in a short flange hanging down beyond the left end of the sleeve. Head and stem are shown schematically and are the flush poppet, held open.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore leaves by the same route as the dose and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26, so that carrier liquid at the pressure of the main line is never presented to an open concentrate port 22 and cannot be driven back toward the concentrate source. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped, so that it removes a film with clean carrier liquid instead of diluting a standing charge of concentrate.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the wearing and sealing parts are replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line. The parts that contact the concentrate are the parts that are exchanged, so a change of concentrate or a worn sealing land is dealt with by fitting a further cartridge rather than by dismantling the installation.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The travel of the piston 28 on this stroke is limited by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46, which sets the measured volume.

9	The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.
10	
11	A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall and so forms an annular space that travels with the piston 28. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.
12	
13	In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20, where it occupies the annular space at the waist 34 and forms a measured volume of concentrate. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall and so forms an annular space that travels with the piston 28. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20, where it occupies the annular space at the waist 34 and forms a measured volume of concentrate. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

input.summary: Fixed every finding from the filing gate. Removed the four unsupported passages from the detailed description (piston-rod actuation sources, the "any form ... such as" broadening of the one-way outlet valve, the materials-selection sentence with its undefined "sealing elements", and the detent and flexible-lip structural variants), narrowed "dose setting indicia" back to the disclosed "dose setting numerals" in claims 9 and 19, the summary, the detailed description, the numeral table and FIG. 4, and dropped "radial" from the carrier-liquid admission port. Rebuilt FIG. 3 so the flush poppet gates the flush bypass at the right with a reachable stem, and so the annulus is one undivided annular rinse channel closed at its right end with the bypass discharging beyond it toward the outlet. Corrected FIG. 4 so the detent recesses and dose setting numerals sit at one station along the collar at three angular positions, and matched the FIG. 4 entry in the Brief Description to the brief. Moved the FIG. 1 inlet and outlet stubs to the extreme axial ends, and gave FIG. 2 the surrounding housing wall and annular gap with the admission port opening into that gap. Every figure brief remains at or below 2800 characters, and no numeral membership changed on any sheet.
reasoning: The four untraced passages were deletions, not rewrites. The description now says only that the piston rod is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke, and says of the one-way outlet valve only what it does: pass liquid from the dose chamber toward the outlet and prevent reverse flow. The ball-and-seat and the detent ball stay where they belong, inside the figure briefs and marked shown schematically, with nothing in the application text existing to justify them.

Deleting the materials paragraph also removed the only appearance of an unnamed 'sealing elements'. I checked the rest of the description for the same defect and found one more loose phrase in the cartridge paragraph, 'the wearing and sealing parts', which now reads that the cartridge is replaced as a unit. No new part is introduced anywhere without a numeral.

The indicia-to-numerals narrowing was made in every place the genus had spread, including the numeral table entry for 54 and the FIG. 4 brief, so the claim term, the description, the table and the sheet all recite the disclosed species. The FIG. 4 patches stay plain and carry no drawing text, since the marks are a depiction convention and the pipeline draws no text into the geometry.

FIG. 3 needed a poppet that both gates the flush bypass and can be reached by the follower pin at the end of the return stroke. The head now sits at a conical seat where the flush bypass turns at the right, the stem runs leftward from that head through an opening in the transverse boss and along the gap above the sleeve, and it ends in a short flange hanging down beyond the sleeve's left end where the pin bears on its right face. Because the return stroke carries the piston leftward, the pin drives flange, stem and head leftward off the seat, so the sequence of contacts is possible and the brief says so in one clause.

The divided-annulus defect was fixed by identifying the upper and lower gaps as one annular rinse channel of the same extent, open at the left to the housing interior and closed at its right end by a hatched transverse boss. The flush bypass now leaves the bore, rises through the upper sleeve band and opens into the housing interior beyond that boss, so rinse liquid travels to the outlet instead of re-entering its own supply. Nothing in the claims or description changed to accommodate this; the text already recited one annular rinse channel between the sleeve and the housing.

For FIG. 4 the collar turns and does not translate, so the three detent recesses and the three dose setting numerals now lie at one station along the collar's length at three angular positions. The engaged recess is the notch broken into the upper outline, the other two are in broken line on the curved surface directly below it, and the numerals are drawn with the middle patch full on the visible surface and the other two running off toward the silhouettes. I replaced the earlier left-and-right wording because left and right on a side view is axial displacement, which is the very error the finding identified.

The Brief Description entry for FIG. 4 was brought into line with the brief rather than adding a housing wall and break line to the sheet, since the collar detail needs no housing and the window already appears on FIG. 1. No numeral moved sheets, so the numeral table, the drawing descriptions and the figure-attribution sentences in the detailed description all stayed synchronized without redistributing labels.

FIG. 1 now opens the inlet stub through the lower housing wall at the extreme left end immediately inboard of the end cap and the outlet stub at the extreme right end immediately inboard of the end wall, which is what claim 12 and the disclosure recite. FIG. 2 gained the housing wall bands and the clear annular gap that FIGS. 1 and 3 show over the same region, and the carrier-liquid admission port now opens into that gap instead of running off the sheet as though carrier liquid came from outside the valve.

Trimming was needed to keep all four briefs at or below 2800 characters after these additions. I removed only wording, never a required body, contact, opening or path: repeated phrases such as ending clear of the drawing area were dropped where the view statement already covers margins, and target lines were shortened while keeping each endpoint on a broad interior region of the intended part.
changes: draft/08-detailed-description.md: deleted the actuation-source clause from the piston rod sentence; deleted the 'any form ... such as' sentence about the one-way outlet valve; deleted the materials and variants paragraph in full; changed 'wearing and sealing parts' to the cartridge; removed 'radial' from the carrier-liquid admission port; 'dose setting indicia' and 'indicium' changed to 'numerals' and 'numeral'.
draft/09-claims.md: claims 9 and 19 now recite dose setting numerals, claim 9 the dose setting numeral.
draft/06-summary.md: indexing paragraph now recites three dose setting numerals.
draft/numerals.md: numeral 54 is now 'dose setting numerals'.
draft/07-drawings.md: FIG. 4 entry is now a fragmentary side view of the index collar and the parts that set and retain the dose, with no broken-away housing wall.
figures/fig-01.md: inlet and outlet stubs moved to the extreme left and right ends of the housing, immediately inboard of the end cap and the end wall.

figures/fig-02.md: added outer housing wall bands above and below the sleeve with a clear annular gap; the concentrate tube now crosses that gap and the upper housing band; the carrier-liquid admission port opens into the gap below the sleeve and is no longer called radial.

figures/fig-03.md: the upper and lower gaps are one annular rinse channel, open at the left and closed at its right end by a hatched transverse boss; the flush bypass leaves the bore, rises through the upper sleeve band and opens into the housing interior beyond the boss toward the outlet, carrying a conical seat at its turn; the flush poppet head sits at that seat with its stem running leftward through the boss to a flange that the follower pin drives leftward as the piston returns; the pin now projects upward from the shaft; target for 58 names the head clear of its seat in the flush bypass and target for 60 names the lower half of the rinse channel.

figures/fig-04.md: the three detent recesses and the three dose setting numerals lie at one station along the collar's length at three angular positions, with the engaged notch broken into the upper outline and the other two recesses in broken line below it; targets for 50 and 54 name the notch broken into the upper outline and the patch full on the visible surface.
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md still lists no references, so the Background carries no citations and none was added in this revision. The claim shape is unchanged apart from the narrowing of the display term from indicia to the disclosed numerals in claims 9 and 19, which reduces scope in a dependent rung only. Claim 1 continues to rest on the combination that the disclosure treats as the invention: the axial ordering of the land faces and port edges that makes concentrate-to-carrier isolation a property of the geometry rather than of a command sequence, together with a flush poppet on the flush bypass that the follower pin on the piston rod opens during the return stroke and that closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port. Removing the deleted description passages does not weaken that position, because none of them was a limitation of any claim; they were open-ended genus statements and variants that broadened the description beyond the inventor's words. Because no search was run, the claims should still be revisited once art is available.

The assertion is also internally inconsistent: if the dose were the annulus at the waist, its volume would be fixed by piston geometry and could not be changed by limiting piston travel, yet ¶41 says "The travel of the piston 28 on this stroke is limited by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46, which sets the measured volume," and claim 7 recites each stop face "limiting travel of the piston to set a respective dose volume."

An inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable measured volume of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid and rinses the surfaces that contacted the concentrate after each dose, without electrical power and without any command additional to the stroke that delivers the dose.

The valve has a housing with an inlet and an outlet and a metering sleeve fixed within the housing. The metering sleeve defines a dose chamber, a concentrate port opening into the dose chamber, a carrier-liquid admission port opening into the dose chamber, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber. A piston slides axially in the dose chamber between a fill position and a discharge position. The piston has an upstream sealing land and a downstream sealing land axially spaced from one another and joined by a reduced-diameter waist.

Separation of the two liquids is enforced by the axial order of the land faces and the port edges rather than by the sequence in which any external command arrives. In the fill position, the waist connects the concentrate port to the dose chamber while the upstream and downstream sealing lands isolate the carrier-liquid admission port from the concentrate port. Movement of the piston toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream sealing land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port. Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume of concentrate and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve toward the outlet. Because one land face has passed the concentrate port before the other land face releases the carrier-liquid admission port, no position of the piston places the concentrate source in communication with the carrier-liquid path.

The rinse is carried out by the return of the same piston. An annular rinse channel lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing, and at least one rinse opening leads from that channel through the metering sleeve into the dose chamber. A follower pin carried by the piston rod opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass during the return stroke, so that carrier liquid sweeps the annular rinse channel, issues from the rinse opening across the surfaces wetted by the concentrate, and leaves through the flush bypass to the outlet. The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port to the dose chamber, so the rinse is complete, and the rinse liquid is on its way to the outlet, before any further concentrate can enter. The rinse cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred, because the element that opens it is the element that carries the piston.

In described embodiments, a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wipes the wall of the dose chamber before the flush poppet opens, so that the flushing stream is presented with a film rather than with standing liquid. Two radial rinse openings are directed across the concentrate port and across the one-way outlet valve, which are the two surfaces on which residue is otherwise retained.

Dose selection is mechanical and self-indexing. An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin, so that each full stroke of the piston turns the index collar by one increment. Three selectable axial stop faces on the index collar limit the travel of the piston and thereby set three dose volumes, a spring-biased detent engaging one of three recesses retains the selected setting, and a transparent window in the housing shows one of three dose setting numerals carried by the index collar, so that the setting is visible without electronics.

A replaceable cartridge contains the piston, the metering sleeve, the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, and is retained by a threaded end cap. Removing the threaded end cap withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the connections at the inlet and the outlet.

A corresponding method admits concentrate to the dose chamber, closes the concentrate port before uncovering the carrier-liquid admission port, expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve, and then opens the flush poppet with the follower pin during the return of the piston and closes it again before the concentrate port is reconnected.

content.text: All seven findings are fixed and the files remain synchronized.

input.summary: Fixed every finding. The description no longer locates the measured volume in the waist annulus: the dose is formed in the dose chamber and its extent is fixed by the travel then permitted to the piston, which agrees with the stop faces of claim 7. The FIG. 3 brief no longer contains an invented actuating train: the transverse boss, the opening through it and the depending flange are gone, the annular rinse channel closes where the sleeve wall meets the housing wall, and the poppet is a conical head with a plain stem on which the follower pin bears. FIG. 1 now shows the inlet and the outlet as axial stubs at opposite ends of the housing, represents the cartridge without an added flange, and keeps the piston rod inside the housing interior short of the end cap. The summary now says the element that opens the rinse is carried by the piston rod. FIGS. 2 and 3 now show the same sleeve, each adding the other view's openings unnumbered. All four briefs remain at or below 2800 characters, and the numeral lists on every sheet are unchanged and still match the drawing descriptions and the FIG. sentences in the detailed description.
reasoning: The dose locus was a drafting inference, not disclosure, and it fought the claimed stop faces. Removing it also meant removing the supporting clause earlier in the description that the waist forms an annular space travelling with the piston, so no sentence anywhere now implies a fixed dose volume set by piston geometry. The description now ties dose size to permitted travel in the same terms as claim 7 and the operation paragraph.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting, so that the index collar 40 is held against vibration and against the forces transmitted through the follower pin 44 until it is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting numerals 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting numeral presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics, without power at the valve and without a controller. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the mechanism itself rather than a stored value, so the displayed setting cannot disagree with the volume that the valve will deliver.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and a flush bypass 26.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20 and carries the film of concentrate remaining on that wall ahead of it, so that the rinse which follows is presented with a wetted surface rather than with standing liquid.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38. Those are the two surfaces on which concentrate is otherwise retained after a dose, the first because concentrate stands in the mouth of the port and the second because concentrate is the last liquid to pass the seat.

The parts that contact the concentrate are the parts that are exchanged, so a change of concentrate or a worn sealing land is dealt with by fitting a further cartridge rather than by dismantling the installation.

-In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The travel of the piston 28 on this stroke is limited by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46, which sets the measured volume.

+In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. An inline liquid metering valve delivers a repeatable measured volume of concentrate into a flowing carrier liquid and rinses the surfaces that contacted the concentrate after each dose, without electrical power and without any command additional to the stroke that delivers the dose.

The valve has a housing with an inlet and an outlet and a metering sleeve fixed within the housing. The metering sleeve defines a dose chamber, a concentrate port opening into the dose chamber, a carrier-liquid admission port opening into the dose chamber, and a flush bypass that opens downstream of the dose chamber. A piston slides axially in the dose chamber between a fill position and a discharge position. The piston has an upstream sealing land and a downstream sealing land axially spaced from one another and joined by a reduced-diameter waist.

Separation of the two liquids is enforced by the axial order of the land faces and the port edges rather than by the sequence in which any external command arrives. In the fill position, the waist connects the concentrate port to the dose chamber while the upstream and downstream sealing lands isolate the carrier-liquid admission port from the concentrate port. Movement of the piston toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port before the downstream sealing land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port. Carrier liquid then enters behind the measured volume of concentrate and expels that volume through a one-way outlet valve toward the outlet. Because one land face has passed the concentrate port before the other land face releases the carrier-liquid admission port, no position of the piston places the concentrate source in communication with the carrier-liquid path.

The rinse is carried out by the return of the same piston. An annular rinse channel lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve and an inner surface of the housing, and at least one rinse opening leads from that channel through the metering sleeve into the dose chamber. A follower pin carried by the piston rod opens a normally closed flush poppet connected to the flush bypass during the return stroke, so that carrier liquid sweeps the annular rinse channel, issues from the rinse opening across the surfaces wetted by the concentrate, and leaves through the flush bypass to the outlet. The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port to the dose chamber, so the rinse is complete, and the rinse liquid is on its way to the outlet, before any further concentrate can enter. The rinse cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred, because the element that opens it is carried by the piston rod itself.

In described embodiments, a flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wipes the wall of the dose chamber before the flush poppet opens, so that the flushing stream is presented with a film rather than with standing liquid. Two radial rinse openings are directed across the concentrate port and across the one-way outlet valve, which are the two surfaces on which residue is otherwise retained.

Dose selection is mechanical and self-indexing. An index collar surrounds the metering sleeve and has a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin, so that each full stroke of the piston turns the index collar by one increment. Three selectable axial stop faces on the index collar limit the travel of the piston and thereby set three dose volumes, a spring-biased detent engaging one of three recesses retains the selected setting, and a transparent window in the housing shows one of three dose setting numerals carried by the index collar, so that the setting is visible without electronics.

A replaceable cartridge contains the piston, the metering sleeve, the one-way outlet valve and the flush poppet, and is retained by a threaded end cap. Removing the threaded end cap withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the connections at the inlet and the outlet.

A corresponding method admits concentrate to the dose chamber, closes the concentrate port before uncovering the carrier-liquid admission port, expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve, and then opens the flush poppet with the follower pin during the return of the piston and closes it again before the concentrate port is reconnected.

# FIG. 1

View: longitudinal sectional view of the inline liquid metering valve, axis horizontal. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges.

Geometry:

- The housing is an elongate cylinder cut lengthwise on its axis, appearing as upper and lower hatched wall bands that run across most of the view and are joined at the right by a hatched end wall. The interior between them is open.
- The left end of the housing is closed by a threaded end cap, drawn as a short hatched ring seated in the left mouth, its outer surface meeting the housing bore along a shallow saw-tooth interface indicating a thread. A plain shaft on the axis extends leftward within the sleeve bore and ends short of the end cap.
- A short tubular stub projects axially leftward from the left end of the housing below the axis, clear of the end cap and the shaft, and opens into the interior; it is the inlet, shown schematically. A second such stub projects axially rightward from the end wall at the right and opens into the interior; it is the outlet, shown schematically. Both stubs end clear of the drawing area.
- The metering sleeve lies inside the housing on the same axis, drawn as an upper hatched band and a lower hatched band spaced inward from the housing wall bands, so that a clear gap is visible above and below it over part of its length, from a position right of the end cap to a position short of the end wall, the sleeve wall meeting the housing wall at the right-hand end of that gap.
- The sleeve, the body in its bore and the parts they carry are drawn as one removable unit, the left end of the sleeve standing against the inner face of the end cap; this unit is the cartridge.
- Within the sleeve bore, in the left half, is a body shown schematically as two hatched enlarged portions joined by a narrower middle portion, the plain shaft running leftward from the left portion.
- A rectangular unhatched panel is set into the upper housing wall band about midway along it, the hatching stopping at its outline; it is the transparent window. Beneath it, on an unnumbered ring surrounding the sleeve in the gap, a small plain patch is visible.

Numerals on this sheet: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 52, 64, 66.

Targets:

- 10: the complete assembly; leader ends just outside the upper housing outline.
- 12: the hatched lower housing wall band, inside the hatching.
- 14: the wall of the left axial stub.
- 16: the wall of the right axial stub.
- 18: the hatched upper band of the sleeve, toward its right.
- 52: the interior of the unhatched rectangular panel.
- 64: the removable unit as a whole; leader ends just outside the left end of the sleeve, clear of all hatching, with an arrowhead directed at the unit.
- 66: the hatched ring in the left mouth of the housing, above the axis.

# FIG. 3

View: enlarged longitudinal section of the metering portion of FIG. 1 during the return stroke, axis horizontal, with the flush poppet held open. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the sheet edges.

Geometry:

- An outer housing wall appears in section as upper and lower hatched bands at the top and bottom of the view. Inside it the sleeve wall appears as upper and lower hatched bands spaced inward, beginning a short way in at the left; the space between them is the bore.
- The clear gap between the sleeve and outer bands, above and below, is one annular rinse channel, open at the left to the housing interior and closed at its right-hand end where the sleeve wall meets the housing wall.
- Left of that meeting a passage leads from the bore up through the upper sleeve band and turns right, through the meeting into the housing interior beyond, which leads to the outlet: the flush bypass, with a conical seat at the turn. A conical head stands clear to the left of that seat, a visible gap between them, with a plain stem extending leftward from the head along the gap above the sleeve toward the piston; head and stem are shown schematically and are the flush poppet.
- In the bore, in the left half, the piston is drawn as two hatched enlarged portions joined by a narrower middle portion. A plain shaft extends leftward on the axis past the sleeve's left end, and a short pin projects upward from it, bearing on the stem of the flush poppet and holding the head clear of its seat.
- At the left edge of the left portion a thin flared projection extends up and left to the upper bore wall and a matching one down and left to the lower: the flexible lip.
- An opening through the upper sleeve band, covered by the left portion, is the concentrate port; a tube rises from it across the gap and the upper outer band.
- Two openings through the lower sleeve band connect the rinse channel to the bore; they are the radial rinse openings. The left lies beneath the concentrate port, aimed at it; the right is aimed at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper band.
- A further opening passes through the lower sleeve band at the right portion of the piston, covered by it; shown unnumbered in this view.

Numerals on this sheet: 22, 26, 28, 44, 56, 58, 60, 62.

Targets:

- 22: interior of the upper opening at the left.
- 26: interior of the flush bypass beyond the seat.
- 28: the piston as a whole; leader ends just outside the outline of the two-land body, clear of all hatching, with an arrowhead directed at it.
- 44: the short pin above the shaft.
- 56: the flared projection at the upper bore wall.
- 58: the conical head clear of its seat in the flush bypass.
- 60: the clear gap between the lower bands.
- 62: the left lower opening.

With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. input.summary: Fixed every finding. The description now attributes the measured volume to the travel available to the piston as fixed by the selected stop face, without naming a stroke, so the fill paragraph and the operation paragraph agree. The detent sentence now says only that the setting is retained until the collar is next indexed; the summary no longer claims operation without electrical power, and the display paragraph says only "without electronics"; the reference to a seat of the one-way outlet valve now names the one-way outlet valve 38; and the FIG. 3 view sentence recites the flush bypass 26 with the definite article. On the sheets, FIG. 1 now shows the sleeve and housing gap over part of the sleeve's length with the sleeve wall meeting the housing wall at the right-hand end of that gap, matching FIG. 3 and the description; the piston rod ends within the sleeve bore short of the end cap; numeral 64 now leads to the removable unit from outside all hatching; numeral 28 in FIG. 3 does the same for the piston; and the FIG. 4 detent spring is shown broken off at its upper end instead of carried by a bracket. All four briefs remain at or below 2800 characters, and the numeral lists, the drawing descriptions and the FIG. sentences in the detailed description are unchanged and still match.
reasoning: The dose-volume conflict was resolved by making both passages speak of travel available to the piston rather than travel on a named stroke, which is as far as the disclosure goes. The fill paragraph already said the extent is fixed by the travel then permitted, so only the operation paragraph needed changing, and claim 7 and its method counterpart continue to read on both without either passage choosing a stroke the inventor never chose.

The detent claim of function shrank to what the inventor wrote. Retention until the next indexing is the disclosed effect; holding against vibration and against the pin forces was drafting embellishment and it also fought the preceding paragraph, where the pin force is exactly what indexes the collar.

The electrical statements now track the source exactly. The inventor tied the absence of electronics to the visibility of the dose setting, so that is the only place the application says it. Nothing now asserts anything about how the piston is driven, which the disclosure never characterises.

The seat reference was replaced with the one-way outlet valve 38 itself. The application text stays shape-neutral about that valve, and the ball-and-seat depiction remains confined to the figure briefs where it is marked shown schematically.

FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 now describe one topology for one annular space. FIG. 3 needs the channel closed at its right-hand end so the flush bypass is the exit for the rinse flow, and the description says the sleeve is spaced from the housing over part of its length, so FIG. 1 was corrected to that same closure rather than the claims or description being adjusted to the earlier drawing.

Numerals 64 and 28 designate assemblies, so they now use the convention FIG. 1 already used for numeral 10: the leader ends outside all hatching with an arrowhead directed at the unit. That keeps 18 the sleeve and 64 the cartridge distinguishable on one sheet, and keeps 28 the whole piston distinct from the land numerals on FIG. 2.

The FIG. 4 bracket was an added support member, not a depiction convention, so it is gone and the coil spring is simply shown broken off at its upper end, which anchors the drawing visually without asserting a part the inventor never described.

FIG. 1 no longer places the shaft's left end in a region the same brief fills with the end cap standing against the sleeve; the shaft now ends within the sleeve bore short of the cap, and the brief says nothing about whether or where the rod leaves the housing.

Both edited briefs needed compression to stay within the character limit after the longer assembly-numeral targets were added. I cut wording only: every body, opening, contact and path in those sheets is still specified, and the remaining targets sit on broad interior regions of their parts.

Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. 33	The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.
34	
35	The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26, so that carrier liquid at the pressure of the main line is never presented to an open concentrate port 22 and cannot be driven back toward the concentrate source. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.
36	
37	Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped, so that it removes a film with clean carrier liquid instead of diluting a standing charge of concentrate.
38	
39	The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the cartridge 64 is replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line.
40	In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.
